summary: @gyomu/ui is a comprehensive component library and abstraction layer that provides a consistent design system for the application. It offers a mix of low-level UI building blocks, declarative form generation systems, and specialized adapters for integrating with Material UI.
responsibilities: Define a unified design system and component library for consistent UI development.
Provide declarative abstractions for dynamic form generation based on data schemas.
Abstract third-party UI framework implementation details via adapter patterns.
Manage reusable form layout and validation strategies.
Standardize interaction patterns through shared provider contexts and component wrappers.

capabilities.name: Design System Components
capabilities.description: Provides a library of atomic and composite UI elements such as avatars, cards, buttons, and inputs.

capabilities.name: Declarative Form Automation
capabilities.description: Enables automatic construction of forms from data schemas with built-in layout orchestration and submission handling.

capabilities.name: Material UI Integration
capabilities.description: Offers standardized wrappers and layout adapters for Material UI, ensuring consistent styling and functional behavior.

capabilities.name: Headless Form Layouts
capabilities.description: Delivers structural components for defining form and field layouts without imposing rigid visual styling.

capabilities.name: Global Interaction Management
capabilities.description: Centralizes management of application-wide UI states such as tooltips and toast notifications.

designDecisions: Uses a layered architecture to separate raw UI components from framework-specific adapters.
Employs a declarative approach for form generation to reduce boilerplate code and ensure schema-driven consistency.
Leverages Tailwind CSS with utility-merging utilities to maintain a highly customizable yet consistent aesthetic.
Uses headless layouts to decouple the structural organization of forms from their visual representation.
usageGuidance: Use components from the primary UI directory for standard application-wide interface building.
Leverage the AutoForm system for complex or repetitive data entry forms to ensure schema-driven consistency.
Prefer the provided MUI adapters when integrating with Material UI to benefit from enforced styling and helper functionality.
Extend or compose headless layout components when building custom UI structures that require specific form field arrangement.
